subtasks.title: Create Test Script for Missing Variables
subtasks.description: Develop a script to simulate missing environment variables.
subtasks.details: Create a script (e.g., a shell script or a Node.js script) that temporarily unsets or overrides the required environment variables. This script will then execute the command `NODE_ENV=production node -e "require('./src/instrumentation').register()"`.
subtasks.testStrategy: The script should execute the command and verify that it throws an error.

subtasks.title: Verify Error on Missing Variables
subtasks.description: Execute the test script and confirm the expected error.
subtasks.details: Run the test script created in the previous step. Observe the output and confirm that the expected error (e.g., an error message indicating a missing environment variable) is thrown.
subtasks.testStrategy: Check the script's output for the expected error message or a non-zero exit code.

subtasks.title: Create Test Script for Present Variables
subtasks.description: Develop a script to simulate all environment variables being present.
subtasks.details: Create a script that sets all required environment variables to valid (though potentially dummy) values. Then, execute the command `NODE_ENV=production node -e "require('./src/instrumentation').register()"`.
subtasks.testStrategy: The script should execute the command and verify that it does NOT throw an error.

subtasks.title: Verify Successful Startup with All Variables
subtasks.description: Execute the test script and confirm successful application startup.
subtasks.details: Run the script from the previous step. Verify that the command executes without errors and that the application starts successfully (e.g., by checking for a specific log message or a successful exit code).
subtasks.testStrategy: Check the script's output for any error messages and verify the application's behavior.

tasks.title: Verify Rate Limiting Functionality
tasks.description: Test the rate limiting functionality.
tasks.details: Manually test the rate limiting by trying to log in 6 times rapidly. The application should block the user after 5 attempts.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually test the rate limiting by attempting to log in multiple times rapidly. Verify that the user is blocked after the configured number of attempts.

subtasks.title: Prepare Test Environment for Rate Limiting
subtasks.description: Ensure the testing environment is set up correctly for rate limiting tests. This includes having a user account available for testing.
subtasks.details: Create or identify a test user account. Ensure the application is running and accessible. Note the login endpoint URL.

subtasks.title: Simulate Rapid Login Attempts
subtasks.description: Simulate rapid login attempts to trigger the rate limiting mechanism.
subtasks.details: Use a tool like `curl` or a browser's developer tools to send multiple login requests in quick succession (e.g., 6 attempts within a short timeframe). Use the test user credentials.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manually attempt to log in multiple times rapidly.

subtasks.title: Verify User Block After Excessive Attempts
subtasks.description: Confirm that the user is blocked after exceeding the allowed login attempts.
subtasks.details: After the rapid login attempts, verify that the user is blocked from logging in. Check for an appropriate error message or behavior (e.g., account lockout).
subtasks.testStrategy: Check for an error message or account lockout after exceeding the login attempt limit.

subtasks.title: Verify Rate Limiting Reset
subtasks.description: Confirm that the rate limiting resets after a certain period.
subtasks.details: Wait for the configured reset period (e.g., 1 minute). Attempt to log in again after the reset period. Verify successful login.
subtasks.testStrategy: Attempt to log in after the reset period and verify successful login.

subtasks.title: Document Test Results
subtasks.description: Document the results of the rate limiting tests.
subtasks.details: Record the steps taken, the expected results, and the actual results. Include screenshots or logs if necessary. Indicate whether the tests passed or failed.

tasks.title: Review and Address Dependency Conflicts
tasks.description: Resolve dependency conflicts if they arise during updates.
tasks.details: If dependency conflicts occur, remove `node_modules` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` and then run `pnpm install`.
tasks.testStrategy: After resolving conflicts, run `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` to ensure the application still functions correctly.

subtasks.title: Identify Dependency Conflicts
subtasks.description: Determine if dependency conflicts exist after updates.
subtasks.details: Run the update process and observe for any error messages related to dependency conflicts. Check the output of the update command for conflict warnings.

subtasks.title: Remove Node Modules and Lockfile
subtasks.description: Remove the node_modules directory and the lockfile to resolve conflicts.
subtasks.details: Delete the `node_modules` directory and `pnpm-lock.yaml` file from the project root.

subtasks.title: Reinstall Dependencies
subtasks.description: Reinstall project dependencies after removing conflicting files.
subtasks.details: Run `pnpm install` to reinstall all dependencies.

subtasks.title: Build the Application
subtasks.description: Ensure the application builds successfully after resolving conflicts.
subtasks.details: Execute the `pnpm build` command and verify that the build process completes without errors.
subtasks.testStrategy: Check the build output for any errors or warnings.

subtasks.title: Run Tests
subtasks.description: Run all tests to confirm application functionality.
subtasks.details: Execute the `pnpm test` command and verify that all tests pass.
subtasks.testStrategy: Ensure all tests pass and that there are no test failures.

tasks.title: Address Type Errors After Strictness Changes
tasks.description: Fix type errors introduced by increased TypeScript strictness.
tasks.details: Fix type errors incrementally, one file at a time. Use `// @ts-expect-error <reason>` temporarily if needed.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the build process and address any type errors that arise. Ensure that all tests pass after the changes.

subtasks.title: Identify Type Errors in a Specific File
subtasks.description: Locate and list all type errors in a designated file.
subtasks.details: Examine the TypeScript compiler output for a specific file, noting the line numbers and error messages.

subtasks.title: Analyze and Understand the First Type Error
subtasks.description: Investigate the root cause of the first identified type error.
subtasks.details: Analyze the code surrounding the first error, considering the types involved and the intended behavior. Determine the reason for the type mismatch.

subtasks.title: Apply a Temporary Fix (if needed)
subtasks.description: Use // @ts-expect-error to temporarily suppress the error if a quick fix isn't immediately apparent.
subtasks.details: If a straightforward fix is not immediately obvious, add a // @ts-expect-error comment with a brief explanation of the issue.

subtasks.title: Implement a Permanent Fix
subtasks.description: Implement a permanent solution to resolve the type error.
subtasks.details: Modify the code to correct the type mismatch. This may involve changing variable types, adjusting function signatures, or updating imports.

subtasks.title: Verify the Fix and Repeat
subtasks.description: Run the build process and repeat the process for the next error.
subtasks.details: Run the TypeScript compiler to ensure the error is resolved. If the error persists, revisit the fix. If all errors are resolved in the file, move to the next file and repeat the process.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the build process to ensure no new type errors are introduced and that all tests pass.

tasks.title: Update Test Snapshots After Updates
tasks.description: Update test snapshots if tests fail after updates.
tasks.details: If tests fail after updates, update test snapshots by running `pnpm test -- -u`.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `pnpm test` and verify that all tests pass after updating the snapshots.

subtasks.title: Run Tests After Updates
subtasks.description: Execute the test suite to identify failing tests after updates.
subtasks.details: Run the command `pnpm test` to execute the test suite and identify any failing tests.

subtasks.title: Identify Failing Tests
subtasks.description: Analyze the test results to determine which tests have failed.
subtasks.details: Examine the output of `pnpm test` to identify the specific tests that have failed. Note the names or descriptions of the failing tests.

subtasks.title: Update Test Snapshots
subtasks.description: Update the test snapshots for the failing tests.
subtasks.details: Run the command `pnpm test -- -u` to update the test snapshots. This command will update the snapshots based on the current state of the application.

subtasks.title: Re-run Tests After Snapshot Updates
subtasks.description: Execute the test suite again to verify the snapshot updates.
subtasks.details: Run the command `pnpm test` again to ensure that all tests, including those that previously failed, now pass after the snapshot updates.

subtasks.title: Verify Test Results
subtasks.description: Confirm that all tests pass after updating snapshots.
subtasks.details: Check the output of `pnpm test` to confirm that all tests have passed. If any tests still fail, investigate the cause and repeat the snapshot update process if necessary.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `pnpm test` and verify that all tests pass after updating the snapshots.

tasks.title: Review Breaking Changes in Package Changelogs
tasks.description: Review breaking changes in package changelogs after updates.
tasks.details: Review breaking changes in package changelogs after updating dependencies. Address any breaking changes or deprecations.
tasks.testStrategy: After addressing breaking changes, run `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` to ensure the application still functions correctly.

subtasks.title: Identify Updated Packages
subtasks.description: Determine which packages have been updated by reviewing the package manager's output or changelogs.
subtasks.details: Examine the output of the update command (e.g., `pnpm update`) or the package manager's logs to identify the specific packages that have been updated. Note the version changes.

subtasks.title: Locate Changelogs
subtasks.description: Find the changelog files or release notes for each updated package.
subtasks.details: For each updated package, search for changelog files (e.g., CHANGELOG.md, Release Notes) or online release notes on the package's website or repository (e.g., GitHub, npm).

subtasks.title: Review Breaking Changes
subtasks.description: Carefully review the changelogs for any breaking changes, deprecations, or compatibility issues.
subtasks.details: Read through the changelogs, paying close attention to sections labeled 'Breaking Changes', 'Deprecations', or similar. Note any changes that might affect the application's functionality or require code modifications.

subtasks.title: Address Breaking Changes
subtasks.description: Implement necessary code changes to address any identified breaking changes or deprecations.
subtasks.details: Based on the information in the changelogs, modify the application's code to accommodate the breaking changes. This may involve updating function calls, adjusting data structures, or replacing deprecated features.

subtasks.title: Verify Functionality
subtasks.description: Test the application after addressing breaking changes to ensure it functions correctly.
subtasks.details: Run `pnpm build` to ensure the application builds without errors. Then, run `pnpm test` to execute all tests and verify that they pass. Manually test critical functionality if necessary.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` to ensure the application still functions correctly.

tasks.title: Rollback if Needed
tasks.description: Rollback changes if issues arise.
tasks.details: If needed, rollback changes by running `git checkout app-next-directory/package.json` and then `pnpm install`.
tasks.testStrategy: After rolling back, ensure the application functions as expected.

subtasks.title: Verify Issue Occurrence
subtasks.description: Determine if a rollback is necessary by identifying the specific issue that triggered the need for rollback.
subtasks.details: Analyze logs, error messages, and user reports to pinpoint the exact problem that necessitates a rollback. Document the issue.

subtasks.title: Checkout package.json
subtasks.description: Execute the git checkout command to revert the package.json file to the previous state.
subtasks.details: Run the command `git checkout app-next-directory/package.json` in the project's root directory. Ensure the command executes without errors.

subtasks.title: Reinstall Dependencies
subtasks.description: Run pnpm install to reinstall dependencies based on the reverted package.json.
subtasks.details: Execute the command `pnpm install` in the project's root directory. Monitor the installation process for any errors or warnings.

subtasks.title: Build the Application
subtasks.description: Run the build process to ensure the application compiles successfully after the rollback.
subtasks.details: Execute the build command, such as `pnpm build`. Check for any compilation errors or warnings.

subtasks.title: Verify Application Functionality
subtasks.description: Test the application's core functionality to confirm the rollback resolved the issue.
subtasks.details: Manually test key features and functionalities of the application. Check for any regressions or unexpected behavior. If possible, run automated tests.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test the application's core functionality to confirm the rollback resolved the issue. Run automated tests if available.
